claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Positron Aerospace Propulsion", series "Acquisition Threat Support", published 2010-03-02 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2009-12-01, DIA document number DIA-08-1003-002. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.
Cover page reads: '2 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-002 / Defense Intelligence Reference Document / Acquisition Threat Support / Positron Aerospace Propulsion'.
Attributed on the DIA list of AATIP/AAWSAP products supplied to the Senate Armed Services Committee to 'Dr Gerald Smith, Positronics Research'.

Released copy runs 35 pages; internal chapter structure covers antimatter, positron air-breathing propulsion, the positron ramjet engine and its UAV, ramjet-assisted missile and single-stage reusable vehicle applications, and solid-core and gas-core positron rockets.

connections.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
connections.note: Tier 2, and the reason is worth stating. A full-text scan of this released DIRD on 23 August 2026 found NO occurrence of the programme name anywhere in the document - unlike 27 of the 32 scanned, whose inside cover names the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program explicitly. The link therefore rests on the DIA's 9 January 2018 list to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which enumerates it among the 38 reference products, and not on the document's own text.

connections.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
connections.note: Positronics Research LLC was an outside small business with no standing DIA relationship; its deliverable reached DIA through the AAWSAP prime contract held by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies. Tier 2 because the contractor name is redacted on the cover page under (b)(3):10 USC 424 and the subcontract itself has not been released.

connections.label: Gerald A. Smith
connections.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Positron Aerospace Propulsion' to 'Dr Gerald Smith, Positronics Research'. Smith is a Yale physics Ph.D., former Penn State physics department head, and developer of the Mark I portable antiproton trap for NASA JPL and the High Performance Antimatter Trap for NASA Marshall; the DIRD subject matter tracks his own NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts study on positron-propelled vehicles.
